To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the AA genotype of the 251A/T SNP of IL8 is associated with protection from the development of CAP and UTI; (2) the AA genotype is associated with protection against the development of severe infection in the setting of UTI; (3) this is associated with increased concentrations of IL-8 in the circulation.
the individualized nature (different for different types of infections) of the significance of the IL8 rs4073 polymorphism in severe infections is associated with a modulated circulating IL8.
carriage of rs10736179 and rs4073 is protective for the development of severe infections in a genotype-specific manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the individualized significance of the rs4073 SNP of IL 8 in severe sepsis and its underlying infection.
the individualized nature and the genetic basis of sepsis.
the identification of genetic polymorphisms that may be of importance for the development of sepsis in an individualized manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 251 A allele of rs4073 is protective from severe infection in patients with UTI and CAP, but not IAI and BBI, and that it is associated with higher concentrations of circulating IL-8 in patients with UT I and CAP.
the 251 A allele of IL 8 is protective in UTI, CAP and sepsis/sepsis shock.
the 251 A allele of IL 8 is associated with a decreased risk for severe infection and that this is associated with a greater production of IL 8.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AA genotype is protective from severe sepsis in UTI but not in other types of severe infection.
the 251 A>T SNP in IL-8 is a genetic risk factor for severe infections.
the 251 A allele is associated with a protective effect against the development of UTIs and CAP, but not against the development of IAI and BBI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the individualized nature is the most important aspect of sepsis and that the genetic profile of the individual patient is a key factor in the pathogenesis of the disease.
genetic variants of the innate immune response can be used as biomarkers to identify patients at risk for severe sepsis.
the individualized nature and the heterogeneity of sepsis should be considered in genetic research.
